english.title: Person in charge of a dog worrying livestock
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), were in charge of a dog which worried livestock, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF LIVESTOCK..), on agricultural land situated at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and (6) of the Dogs (Protection of Livestock) Act 1953.

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies after 17/03/2026 due to changes made by the Dogs (Protection of Livestock) (Amendment) Act 2025. For the offence of person in charge of a dog attacking/worrying livestock under section 1 of the Dogs (Protection of Livestock) Act 1953 applying after this date, see H102637.(ii) IMPORTANT - Under section 2(1), a prosecution for this offence requires the consent of either the occupier of the land, the owner of any of the livestock involved or the consent of the Chief Constable or his Deputy (there seems to be no provision for this authority to be delegated). If no other system is in place, add the following wording, filled in as far as possible by you, to the front of the file for the Chief Constable/Deputy Chief Constable to sign:

I (name of Chief Constable/ Deputy Chief Constable) AS CHIEF CONSTABLE/DEPUTY CHIEF CONSTABLE DESIGNATE OF (police force) CONSENT TO THE PROSECUTION OF (name of offender) OF (address of offender) FOR ALLOWING HIS DOG TO WORRY LIVESTOCK CONTRARY TO SECTION 1(1) AND SECTION 1(6) OF THE DOGS (PROTECTION OF LIVESTOCK) ACT 1953 ON (specify date) AT (specify township) WHICH IS WITHIN THIS POLICE FORCE AREA.

SIGNED DATE

(iii) Also consider:H568 - owner of a dog worrying livestock,H569 - dog not under proper control (complaint only),
H11472 - owner / person in charge of dog dangerously out of control causing injury
H11473 - owner / person in charge of a dog dangerously out of control - no injury
